subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw split this umbrella into native tool batching, context block lifecycle, and plan enforcement tracks, and which of those should be core runtime/API work versus plugin or ClawHub work?
rationale: The request adds native tool schemas, persisted context semantics, config surface, and runner enforcement policy; repository policy treats these as compatibility- and product-sensitive decisions rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Split Into Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Route To Narrower Issues
options.body: Use the open context-clearing and workflow-safety issues for their portions and track only native batch tooling here or in a new issue.

options.title: Reject Core Orchestration Expansion
options.body: Close or narrow the umbrella if maintainers decide AI-managed context blocks and strict plan gating are too much heavy orchestration for core.

recommendation.title: Split Into Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history across planning, strict-agentic execution, web search, and context-pruning docs, making him the best available routing owner for the product split.
